biography.plain_text: Ludovico Spada Veralli Potenziani was an Italian agricultural landowner and politician who inherited substantial family estates around Rieti. As governor of Rome under the Fascist regime, he oversaw major public works before becoming a senator. The son of Senator Giovanni Potenziani, he later presided over the International Institute of Agriculture.

long_biography.plain_text:
Ludovico Spada Veralli Potenziani made land available to Nazareno Strampelli for experiments in wheat breeding. He also led the Sabine agricultural association, which promoted field trials of chemical fertilisers. His support gave the researcher a local base for work on improving grain yields.

After flooding struck his home region in 1923, Potenziani presented Mussolini with proposals for the area's recovery. He subsequently promoted drainage works and industrial development, including an artificial-silk factory. He also worked with aviation entrepreneur Giambattista Caproni on the construction of the Terminilluccio cable car, adding mountain transport to his regional projects.

Identity is secure through the existing encyclopaedia endpoint and concordant primary records. The recorded age 90 matches death age. Similar earlier family names, including the nineteenth-century banker, are not used as this person's career.

The original agricultural wealth premise comes from productive estates, personal property attribution and explicit parental succession. Political office, government infrastructure and factories he encouraged are not automatically personal assets.

Terminal rural operations survived, but the residual estate included urban property and had declined. Its internal weights are unestablished, so Agriculture is an explicit origin-sector fallback. No exact wealth estimate or company total is assigned.
